The Chinese Fused a Ford Bronco With a Tesla and Won a Design Award. Nail or Fail?
10 photos
Photo: Chery
You know the Chinese. They slap a copycat design onto a model in development, come up with some headlights and taillights that they saw on American or European cars, and roll out a new car. Sure, not all cars built in China are impersonators, but this Chery iCaur V23 wants to be.
Chery openly admitted that they built a Ford Bronco- and Tesla Model S-inspired SUV, which saw the light of day under the auto giant's dedicated new energy sub-brand, originally launched as iCAR. However, it eventually changed its name to iCaur to avoid a trademark and copyright dispute with Apple.
Chery Automobile’s Vice President and design head, Dr. Su Jun, explicitly cited the ICE -powered Ford Bronco SUV and the electric Tesla Model S sedan as the two core inspirations behind the entire V lineup , and the V23 makes no exception.
The goal was to blend the best of two worlds in a single vehicle: zero tailpipe emissions and a quiet ride from the sleek Tesla sedan with the rugged stance and the tall, upright riding position from the boxy Bronco off-roader.
Photo: Chery The V23 features a retro, rugged, and squared-off silhouette, similar to classic military vehicles and iconic off-roaders like the Bronco (who would have guessed?). The most obvious Bronco nod is the front fascia, complete with the Bronco's signature circular headlights, flanked by horizontal, bar-shaped LED daytime running lights extending outward.
It comes with the ultra-flat hood, perfectly vertical side panels, and slab-sided doors, with completely flush door handles, mimicking the Tesla-like minimalism in this regard. However, it is not exactly a clone, but more of a mashup, looking like it also stole some flair from the Land Rover Defender and the Suzuki Jimny.
Instead of a full-size spare tire on the back, it features a small, integrated rectangular external storage box that looks like a miniature retro lunchbox or a futuristic tech pod, which Chery officially refers to as the "functional backpack." It is designed to offer drivers a storage space for the charging cable.
As hard as it may be to believe, the iCaur V23 won the highly prestigious German Red Dot Design Award: Design Concept 2026. Referred to as the "Oscar of Design," this particular win is quite a success for Chery’s sub-brand.
Photo: Chery The formula has proven highly successful in the V23’s domestic market, where it sold roughly 100,000 units within just one year. While the iCaur V23 has surpassed the 100,000 global sales mark across roughly 20 international markets (primarily in China, Southeast Asia, South Africa, and the Middle East), its European rollout is just beginning. Chery has no plans to bring the model stateside or any model of the iCaur brand, for that matter.
The T esla Model S /Ford Bronco mashup, the Chery iCaur V23 starts at 99,800 yuan, which translates to roughly $13,700. The absolute cheapest new car available on the American market is the Nissan Versa, which carries an MSRP of $16,500.
For the money, customers go home in a V23 RWD with a single rear-mounted permanent magnet synchronous motor, which produces 134 horsepower (136 metric horsepower) and 133 pound-feet (180 Newton meters) of torque. It accelerates from 0 to 62 mph (0 to 100 kph) in 11.0 seconds and maxes out at 87 mph (140 kph).
A lithium iron phosphate (LFP) battery pack with a capacity of 59.93 kWh stores enough energy for a drive of up to 249 miles (401 kilometers) under the very generous CLTC standard, before the EV needs to be plugged in again.
Photo: Chery In the meantime, the range-topping variant, the high-performance iCaur Super V23 Series, which starts at 174,800 yuan ($24,600), comes with a dual-motor setup and all-wheel drive. The system pushes out 449 horsepower (455 metric horsepower) and 361 pound-feet (490 Newton meters) of torque.
The setup makes the iCaur Super V23 Series sprint from 0 to 62 mph (0 to 100 kph) in just 4.5 seconds, inching closer to supercar territory, and top out at 106 mph (170 kph), which is inching further from supercar territory.
The range-topping version rolls off the production line of Chery’s primary smart factory in Wuhu, China, sporting the 80.16-kWh Nickel-manganese-cobalt (NMC) battery pack supplied by CATL, securing a range of up to 311 miles (501 kilometers).
Chery has no plans to sell its V lineup in the United States but is currently testing the waters. Besides, up until now, the United States has effectively blocked Chinese electric vehicles through 100%+ tariffs and a looming ban on Chinese-developed connected software and hardware. To bypass all these restrictions, Chery will need to hunt an American partner. Ford Authority reported that the hunt has already started.
While the U.S. remains a long-term goal, Chery is using Canada as its immediate operational testing ground. Canada adjusted its strict tariff restrictions on Chinese EVs, opening a legal framework that allows low-tariff imports on a capped number of vehicles annually.
